analysis: Changed behavior: provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/SwitchCommand.swift (head lines 36-37) now calls ModelScanner.configureCacheDirectory(snapshot.configuredModelCacheDirectory) after loadRuntimeSnapshot(configPath:) and before scanAllModels, so `darkbloom switch --model/--all` scans the running daemon's configured model_cache_directory rather than the default cache. The change is a functional bug fix (issue #1469). The directory comes from the operator's own provider.toml, which is the same trust domain as the existing config path taken from the daemon state file. The unchanged requireLiveState and process-identity checks (head lines 29-33, 56-59), the mailbox request and the daemon-side validation and hashing stay in place. The chosen models are still filtered by EngineV2SupportedModels and ModelRuntimeRequirements.isEligible, and the daemon re-validates artifacts before switching. A local attacker who can write provider.toml could already redirect the model cache (T-012, TB-003); this PR adds no new capability and does not weaken weight-hash verification as far as the supplied evidence shows. The scan only enumerates model IDs and does not change the cache storage, encryption or prefix-cache (T-041) paths. The docs change in docs/provider/cli-reference.md is a one-line statement that matches the code; the other displayed sections are unchanged context. The new test in SwitchCommandTests.swift runs in a sandbox and touches no production code. Unverified: ModelScanner.configureCacheDirectory is process-global state, and its validation of absolute or relative paths (including symlink handling) is outside the supplied evidence. Because the CLI is a short-lived process, I see no cross-request leakage. No regression is identified.
